$comment: The one set of versions an agent machine runs together. buzz-acp (Buzz's headless harness, from the block/buzz release bundle) speaks one ACP protocol, and the npm adapters must speak it too: a newer adapter's SDK rejected buzz-acp 0.5.30's initialize (protocolVersion 2 with clientInfo; SDK 2.0.1+ wants info). machine/setup.sh carries these values as shell variables; scripts/check-machine-pins.mjs (in npm run check) fails when setup.sh, its comments or machine/tests disagree with this file. To move any of them, move them together here and in setup.sh, and check the initialize handshake on a machine first. The CLIs below are what the adapters run and what agentctl signs in with; their pins are checked the same way.

harness.name: buzz-acp
harness.source: block/buzz release bundle, vendored by hand on each machine

@openai/codex.handshake: buzz-acp 0.5.30 initialize -> codex-acp 2.2.2 protocolVersion 1; session/new answers Authentication required until signed in

grok.source: https://x.ai/cli/grok-1.0.70-macos-aarch64.gz (xAI publishes no checksum; hash of the tested download)
grok.command: grok agent --always-approve stdio (Buzz 0.5.30 Grok Build preset)
grok.handshake: buzz-acp 0.5.30 initialize -> grok 1.0.70 protocolVersion 1; session/new answers Authentication required until signed in

@qwen-code/qwen-code.command: qwen --acp --approval-mode yolo --auth-type openai, with OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_MODEL in the environment
@qwen-code/qwen-code.handshake: buzz-acp 0.5.30 initialize -> qwen-code 0.27.4 protocolVersion 1; session/new answers -32000 Authentication required with no key in the environment, and opens a session with any key there (Qwen Code does not check it; agentctl does, with GET /models). Checked on the Commerce Mac, 2026-11-16
